prompt: When an oceanic plate collides with a continental plate, why is it usually the oceanic plate that sinks into the mantle?

options.text: Oceanic lithosphere is denser than the continental lithosphere and the underlying asthenosphere it sinks into
Oceanic plates are thinner, and thin plates always sink first
Seawater on top of the oceanic plate weighs it down below the continent
Continental plates are anchored to the core and cannot move downward

explanation: Oceanic lithosphere is made of dense basaltic rock and, as it cools, becomes denser than the asthenosphere below, so it sinks in subduction while more buoyant continental crust resists sinking.
